summary: Elevated TTFB on chat completions after runtime & model upgrade
description:
Issue summary: Customer reports a significant increase in time-to-first-token (TTFB) for chat completion requests following the runtime and model variant upgrade deployed 2026-03-02. Impact: Elevated TTFB (~2-4s) on streaming chat completions for high-volume endpoints, causing perceived slowness in customer-facing chat UI and some client-side timeouts. Environment: Production (us-east-1); customer account pinned to enterprise dedicated capacity. Observed behavior: Median TTFB increased from ~180ms to ~2.1s for redwood-3b-v2; p95 moved from ~420ms to ~3.8s. Expected behavior: TTFB should remain sub-500ms for these request profiles. Temporary impact: Customer experiencing user-visible latency spikes and intermittent streaming disconnects.

Request IDs/examples included below and in logs field.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use customer API key and send a chat.completions request with streaming enabled against model redwood-3b-v2 (same payload used in production).
2) Observe initial chunk arrival time (TTFB) vs previous baseline from Feb 28 snapshot.
3) Repeat across several concurrent clients to reproduce higher percentile TTFB (p95/p99).
investigation_notes: 2026-03-03 10:12: Correlated spike with runtime release 'runtime-2.14.0' and model routing change that started 2026-03-02 23:00 UTC.

Observed two patterns: (A) cold-activity TTFB increase when KV cache miss occurs; (B) increased kernel selection overhead on specific sequence-length distributions after new kernel selection logic rolled out.
Tracing shows additional 1.6s spent in 'kernel_select' + 'lazy_kv_init' paths for affected requests (trace ids: trace-0a1b2c, trace-0d3e4f).
Autoscaler and GPU utilization do not show resource exhaustion; dedicated pool healthy. No increase in 5xx rates during window.
Hypothesis: runtime-2.14.0 introduced a change that defers KV cache warmup and added a synchronous kernel selection step on first token that is now on the critical path for streaming TTFB.
Cross-referenced with SUP-25485 and SUP-25486 (similar customer reports after upgrade); likely common root cause in runtime kernel/kv path.
Reached out to runtime team; Eng oncall (Liam Chen) engaged and created INT-412 to track root cause and code-level fix.
logs: 2026-03-03T09:58:23Z request_id=req-83a1 TTFB=2.14s model=redwood-3b-v2 routing_variant=rv-2026-03-02 kernel_select_ms=1600 lazy_kv_init_ms=520
2026-03-03T10:01:11Z request_id=req-87b5 TTFB=3.02s model=llama-2-13b-chat routing_variant=rv-2026-03-02 kernel_select_ms=2100 lazy_kv_init_ms=700

Stacktrace snippets: serving_runtime/select_kernel.go: line 214 (synchronous selection path)
serving_runtime/kv_cache.go: line 88 (lazy init path)
No 5xx spikes; all responses returned 200 but with delayed streaming first token.
resolution_notes: 2026-03-03 12:40 - Temporary mitigation: Rolled back runtime kernel selection change in a canary pool for the customer's dedicated capacity and observed TTFB return to baseline (~180-240ms).
2026-03-03 14:05 - Implemented emergency routing policy to pin Acme Analytics traffic to the legacy runtime variant until definitive fix is deployed (change id: route-change-6721).

Planned fix: runtime team to make kernel selection non-blocking for first-token path or precompute selection during request enqueue; also add proactive KV warmup for long-lived sessions. Target patch release: 2026-03-05.
Post-incident follow-up: add a perf gating test to CI comparing TTFB before runtime releases and alerting if median TTFB regresses >20%.
